task.description: Security review of the ISS-0047 fix in lib/letflow/identity.ex (commit 548c338 on branch feature/WF03-ISS0047-20260818). This touches the tenant-scoped identity/JIT-provisioning path (insert_or_fetch/4 and new helpers username_unique_conflict?/1, get_by_username/2, identity_matches?/2). The new get_by_username/2 helper queries users by username within a caller-supplied :prefix (per-tenant Postgres schema, Decision 0006). Verify this does not introduce a cross-tenant leak, an identity-confusion vector, or an authentication bypass -- specifically: could identity_matches?/2's comparison ever incorrectly treat two DIFFERENT external identities as the same, letting an attacker-controlled JIT provisioning request resolve to (and thus authenticate as) another user's existing account? Check security-invariants.md's INV list for anything applicable to identity/auth paths.
acceptance_criteria: get_by_username/2 is correctly scoped to the same :prefix (tenant schema) as the rest of insert_or_fetch/4 -- no cross-tenant query possible.
identity_matches?/2's comparison logic cannot be satisfied by two genuinely different external identities (verify the exact fields compared and their semantics).
The fix does not create a path where an unauthenticated or wrong caller can cause provision_oidc_user/4 to resolve to an existing, unrelated user's account (account-takeover-via-race check).
No new information disclosure (e.g. username existence across tenants) introduced.
Applicable security-invariants.md INV items checked explicitly, not assumed satisfied.
